<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="ShakespeareFan00" /></noinclude><section begin=par117 />''down (with) rivers of water''; 1:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=136}}; so also {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ|translate=to run over with, to flow with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָזַל}} to gush out with, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָטַף|translate=to drop, to overflow with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=18}}a; {{GHGheb|text=פָּרַח|translate=to break forth}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁטַף|translate=to overflow}}, but also (transitively) ''to overflow with'', probably in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=נוּב|translate=to bud with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=31}}; so perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=עָבַר|translate=to pass over, to overflow with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא|translate=to go forth}} with, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=3}}.—Especially bold, but still on the analogy of the above examples, is {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=6}}, where it is said of a vineyard {{GHGheb|text=וְעָלָה שָׁמִיר וָשָׁ֫יִת|translate=but it shall come up}} (it shall be overgrown) ''with briers and thorns''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=31}}, and still more boldly, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|aa}}
With the opposite idea, {{GHGheb|text=חָסֵר|translate=to be in want of, to lack}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכֹל|translate=to be bereaved of}} (as though it were ''to lose''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=45}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=17}} even {{GHGheb|text=הַמְעַט־לָ֫נוּ}} (prop. ''was there too little for us of ...?'') as being equivalent to a verbum inopiae (= ''had we too little of'' ...?) is construed with an accusative; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=32}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|bb}}
(''c'') Several verbs of ''dwelling''; the accusative in this case expresses either the place or the thing ''at'' which or ''with'' which any one tarries; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=4}} after {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}}, cf. {{GHGpar|118|g}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=14}} after {{GHGheb|text=גּוּר}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=57|verse=5}} after {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַב}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=16}} with {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַן}}; or even the person (the people) with whom any one dwells or is a guest, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=120|verse=5|hidebook=1}} after {{GHGheb|text=גּוּר}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=20}} after {{GHGheb|text=זָבַל}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=19}} with {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַן}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|cc}}
'''5'''. ''Two accusatives'' (usually one of the person and one of the thing) are governed by—

(''a'') The causative conjugations ({{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, sometimes also ''Pilpel'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כִּלְכֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=12}}, &c.) of verbs which are simply transitive in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, and hence also of {{GHGterm|verba induendi}} and ''exuendi'', &c. (cf. above a and u, and also y, z), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=הַרְאֵ֫נִי נָא אֶת־כְּבֹדֶ֫ךָ|translate=show me, I pray thee, thy glory}}. Thus very frequently {{GHGheb|text=הוֹדִיעַ|translate=to cause}} some one ''to know'' something; {{GHGheb|text=לִמַּד|translate=docere aliquem aliquid}}, &c.; cf. further, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=42}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּלְבֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ בִגְדֵי־שֵׁשׁ|translate=and he caused him to put on vestures of fine linen}} (''he arrayed him in vestures'', &c.); cf. in the opposite sense, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=23}} (both accusatives after {{GHGheb|text=הִפְשִׁיט}} introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אֶת}}); so with {{GHGheb|text=מִלֵּא|translate=to fill, to fill up}} with something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִזֵּר|translate=to gird}} some one with something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=עִטֵּר|translate=to crown}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=8|verse=6}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=חִסֵּר|translate=to cause}} some one ''to lack'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=8|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽאֱכִיל|translate=to feed}} some one with something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=32}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁקָה|translate=to make}} some one ''drink'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=32}} ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|dd}}
(''b'') Many verbs (even in {{GHGterm|Qal}}) which express an influence upon the object through some external means. The latter, in this case, is attached as a second object. They are especially—

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|ee}}
(α) Verbs which express ''covering, clothing, overlaying'', {{GHGheb|text=חָגַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=צִפָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=29}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=טוּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=10}} ff., {{GHGheb|text=עָטַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=13}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=רָגַם אֶבֶן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=25}}, &c.; hence also verbs which express ''sowing'' ({{GHGheb|text=זָרַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jud|chapter=9|verse=45}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=10}} 30:23), ''planting'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=2}}), ''anointing'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=8}}) ''with'' anything.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|ff}}
(β) Expressions of ''giving'', thus {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=19}} where the accusative of the thing precedes; ''endowing'', {{GHGheb|text=זָבַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=20}}; and its opposite ''taking away'', as {{GHGheb|text=קָבַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֵּרַךְ|translate=to bless some one with something}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=14}}; ''to give graciously'', {{GHGheb|text=חָנַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=5}}; ''to sustain'' (i.e. to support, to maintain, to furnish) ''with'' anything,<section end=par117 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
